claims.cards/alternating_dumbbell_curl.json#c2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand (palms-forward) grip, arms hanging by the sides.
claims.cards/barbell_curl.json#c1: Grip the bar underhand (palms up), hands about shoulder-width apart, so the wrists, elbows and shoulders line up.
claims.cards/barbell_curl.json#c8: Keep the wrists straight during the lift; bent wrists put extra load on them and can lead to discomfort.
claims.cards/cable_curl.json#c1: Attach a bar to the low pulley, take an underhand (palms-up) grip about shoulder-width apart, and step back from the stack.
claims.cards/cable_curl.json#c9: Inferred from the dumbbell curl: keep the wrists straight; bent wrists add load to them and can cause discomfort.
claims.cards/cross_body_hammer_curl.json#c1: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, feet about shoulder-width apart, dumbbells in front of you with the palms facing the body.
claims.cards/dumbbell_biceps_curl.json#c1: Hold the dumbbells with a closed, palms-forward (supinated) grip, thumbs wrapped round the handles, arms hanging at the sides.
claims.cards/ez_bar_curl.json#c1: Hold the EZ bar underhand on its angled sections, which is easier on the wrists.
claims.cards/ez_bar_curl.json#c2: From a study discussion, not a measured result (Coratella 2023 tested a cable bar and rope, not an EZ bar): the EZ grip is semi-supinated (half-way between palms up and palms in) rather than neutral, and the hands sit closer together than on a straight bar to fit the natural angle of the elbow.
claims.cards/ez_bar_curl.json#c8: Keep the wrists straight during the lift; bent wrists put extra load on them and can lead to discomfort.
claims.cards/incline_dumbbell_curl.json#c11: Inferred from the seated dumbbell curl (same grip, back supported): take a closed grip, palms forward with thumbs wrapped; keep the wrists straight; keep the head, shoulders and buttocks against the bench; bent wrists add load and can cause discomfort.
claims.cards/preacher_curl.json#c1: Sit at the preacher bench and set the seat height so the chest and upper arms touch the pad; take the curl bar with an underhand grip.
claims.cards/preacher_curl.json#c8: Keep the wrists straight and the chin tucked; bent wrists add load to them and can cause discomfort.
claims.cards/reverse_curl.json#c1: Grip the bar overhand (palms down), hands about shoulder-width apart, in a straight line with the shoulders and elbows.
claims.cards/reverse_curl.json#c6: Keep the wrists neutral: you should be able to draw a straight line from the hands to the elbows.
claims.cards/single_arm_lat_pulldown.json#c15: In 20 healthy adults squeezing a hand dynamometer, grip was strongest with the wrist in the position they chose themselves (about 35 degrees bent back) and weaker when the wrist was moved 10 to 15 degrees away from it in any direction, including curled forward (flexion). Applied to holding a bar or handle by reasoning, not measured on this exercise.
Single handle (c1). Neither technique source names a palm direction, so none is sourced here.

claims.cards/single_arm_triceps_pushdown.json#c: Attach a single handle and grip it firmly with a full grip, thumb wrapped round the handle.
The wrist stays neutral, in line with the forearm, throughout.
claims.cards/single_arm_triceps_pushdown.json#g: One handle, full grip. The sources read do not say which way the palm faces; the drawing should use the plain handle hold without claiming an orientation.
claims.cards/skull_crusher.json#c1: Closed grip with thumbs wrapped, palms toward the feet; lie on a flat bench with feet firmly on the floor.
claims.cards/skull_crusher.json#c3: Keep the wrists neutral, neither bent forward nor back.
claims.shared/curl.json#appliesTo: dumbbell_biceps_curl, alternating_dumbbell_curl, barbell_curl, ez_bar_curl, hammer_curl, cross_body_hammer_curl, cable_curl, bayesian_cable_curl, preacher_curl, incline_dumbbell_curl, concentration_curl, reverse_curl
claims.shared/curl.json#c1: For dumbbell curls, take a closed grip with the thumbs wrapped round the handles.
claims.shared/curl.json#c2: The hammer curl uses the same closed grip with the thumbs round the handles, palms facing the body.
claims.shared/curl.json#c3: Keep the wrist neutral through the curl: avoid bending it forward (flexion) or back (extension).
claims.shared/curl.json#c4: Keep the wrists straight during the curl; bent wrists put unnecessary load on them and can lead to discomfort or injury.
claims.shared/curl.json#c5: Because elbow structure differs, some people cannot hold the dumbbells against their sides at the bottom without bending the wrist; choose the dumbbell position that keeps the wrist straight with the forearm.
claims.shared/rope-rule.json#c1: For the rope pushdown, hold the rope with each hand up against its clubbed end (the knob).
claims.shared/rope-rule.json#c2: Grasp the handle or rope firmly with a full grip, thumbs clasped around it.
claims.shared/rope-rule.json#c3: For the overhead extension the rope is held with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) behind the head. Using the same neutral grip for the rope pushdown is an inference: no source read states the palm direction for the pushdown.
claims.shared/rope-rule.json#c4: In the rope pushdown the wrists stay straight for the whole movement, in line with the forearms.
claims.shared/rope-rule.json#c6: Bending the wrists (flexing them) as you push the weight down moves work from the triceps to the forearms, puts the wrists at a mechanical disadvantage and stresses the elbow; keep the wrists neutral. The source says this happens especially with the bar attachment; applying it to the rope is an inference.
